lane: off-catalogue fault discovery for the DOE GEMS Prize (DrivenData 306)
ranking_basis: expected DTI improvement per unit implementation cost, judged before measurement

items.name: H67-A Cartographic-gap faults (SGMC derivative)
items.signature: Not an edge or curvature transform at all: a set-membership test. A pixel is a fault contact drawn on a Nevada state geologic map but absent from the USGS Quaternary fault and fold database and from INGENIOUS, which is exactly what labels.tif is built from.
items.why_off_catalogue: The problem page states the labels come from the USGS quaternary fault maps and INGENIOUS, and that the test faults were expert-identified and are not in the current public USGS database. QFDB is Quaternary-only, so bedrock geologic-map faults are structurally omitted from it. Measured: 79,615 of 83,593 SGMC fault pixels (95.2%) lie outside the given catalogue and 62,122 are more than 300 m from it.
items.named_mimic: Map-unit contacts and bedding traces digitised as 'faults' with no geomorphic expression; map-index and quadrangle boundary lines; lithologic boundaries.
items.differs_from_repo: No earlier session in this family emitted an SGMC-anchored candidate. registry/data_manifest.json carries the SGMC raster explicitly annotated 'proxy only; not used in the factorial'.
items.cost: Low - the layer is already in the pinned mirror; no new external data required.
items.status: implemented and held out this session

measured_outcome.result: On instrument C (withheld catalogue segments, 62,383 pooled positives, 2 folds) adding the SGMC layers to catalogue distance changed HOLDOUT-DTI by exactly 0.0000: R1 0.0178, R4 0.0178, R5 0.0178, CI95 [0.0147,0.0208] for all three. On instrument N (withheld SGMC-off segments) R2 scored 0.0000 because the 300 m segment buffer removes every visible pool pixel within 300 m of the truth, so the feature cannot see it. The cartographic gap is real (95.2% off-catalogue) but it carries no measurable incremental predictive signal for withheld faults on either instrument.

items.name: H67-B Metric-native maximal-coverage emission
items.layers: any belief surface; no new input layer
items.signature: Greedy maximisation of the expected official DTI itself under an independent-Bernoulli truth model, with an exact closed form for the per-dot expected kernel credit. Replaces a fixed dot budget plus Poisson-disk thinning.
items.why_off_catalogue: It does not change which faults are believed; it changes how much of the alpha=0.2 budget is wasted on redundant dots. The calibration inversion gives x = (N-M)/|G| = 0.676 for the best prior family, i.e. two thirds of a truth-set's worth of emitted mass earns nothing.
items.named_mimic: None - this is a placement rule, not a geological signal. Its failure mode is over-thinning, which the break-even rule bounds.
items.differs_from_repo: Earlier sessions fix a dot count and then thin; none optimises the metric's own expectation, and none derives the per-dot expected credit in closed form.
items.cost: Low - 180 lines plus unit tests, already written and Monte-Carlo verified.

measured_outcome.result: Metric-native greedy emission of 45,000 binary dots. HOLDOUT-DTI 0.17898, CI95 [0.17816,0.17980] on instrument C, versus a 0.0707 uniform-random placement null and a 0.0729 lattice null on the same eligible mask and budget: a 2.53x null-adjusted lift. This is the recipe that was emitted, validated and published.

items.name: H67-C Thermal-spring step-out
items.layers: gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv (27,092 points with measured temperature) + cond_surf + depth_to_base_surf
items.signature: Points where measured spring temperature exceeds 40 C but the nearest mapped fault is more than 300 m away: the fault implied by the discharge but not drawn.
items.why_off_catalogue: Geothermal discharge is structurally controlled by permeable fault zones; a hot spring in a valley floor away from any mapped trace implies an unmapped or blind conductor. Neither QFDB nor INGENIOUS is built from spring chemistry.
items.named_mimic: Artesian and mine water, deep-circulation non-fault flow, conductivity anomalies from clay caps, and temperature values that are measured at depth rather than at the surface.
items.differs_from_repo: The well/spring CSV is fetched in this repo but its dist_known_fault_px column is explicitly excluded as label-derived and the points have never been used as an emission target.
items.cost: Low - the CSV is already pinned.

measured_outcome.status: NOT TESTED - blocked on data access
measured_outcome.result: Needs GDR thermal-spring attributes beyond the mirrored CSV; the three GDR CSVs that are reachable all carry a label-derived dist_known_fault_px column, so they are unusable as features (leakage).

items.name: H67-D Basement-step corridors
items.signature: Linear corridors of abrupt cover-thickness change: a normal fault in a basin produces a step in basement depth that survives 4-6 km of fill and leaves no surface scarp.
items.why_off_catalogue: Buried basin-margin faults are the classic population that surface-mapping compilations omit entirely, and they are the ones a geophysical inversion recovers.
items.named_mimic: Paleochannels, alluvial-fan edges, volcanic flow margins, and inversion artefacts at survey-line ties.
items.differs_from_repo: basement_step is computed here for the first time; prior sessions used the raw band only.
items.cost: Low-medium - the layer is built; it needs its own holdout arm.
items.status: layer built, not yet held out alone

measured_outcome.result: Rank 4 on cost/benefit; the geophysics-only stack already contains the gravity and magnetic gradient layers this hypothesis would add, and it is the stack that produced the 0.17898 result, so a separate basement-step experiment was not worth a slot.

items.name: H67-E Strike-concordant LiDAR scarp chains
items.layers: lidar_step_max, lapneg/lappos asymmetry, coh100, strike + the 100 m structure tensor
items.signature: A scarp is a step with a consistent down-face direction; a fault is strike-coherent over hundreds of metres while terrace risers and channel banks are not. The concordance term is cos^2 of the angle between the 1 m-derived scarp strike and the local structure-tensor orientation.
items.why_off_catalogue: Subtle, short, discontinuous scarps are exactly what a field geologist adds and what a Quaternary-only compilation misses.
items.named_mimic: Fluvial terrace risers, natural channel banks, landslide headscarps, shorelines, roads and canals, and DEM tile seams.
items.differs_from_repo: The inherited lidar_lane session used the same layers but its reported advantage was reversed by relief-matched analysis and its dot set failed the raw uniqueness threshold. This variant adds the strike-concordance term and the metric-native emitter.
items.cost: Blocked at the requested scale: raw 1 m 3DEP tiles are not reachable from this sandbox, so the filters can only run at 200-2000 m on the 100 m aggregate. Named free official source if that changes: USGS 3DEP 1 m via The National Map (public domain).
items.status: layers built at 100 m; native-resolution run blocked (IR-67-SCALE-01)

measured_outcome.status: BLOCKED - native-resolution lidar is not obtainable here
measured_outcome.result: Egress is limited to github.com / api.github.com / pypi.org, so USGS 3DEP and the DrivenData 1 m DEM links return HTTP 000 (IR-66-DATA-01). Only the owner-derived 100 m lidar_scarp_features_u8 layer exists; its lapneg/lappos/relief channels reached AUC 0.580-0.587 in the leakage canary, i.e. weak but not leakage.

outcome.decisive_finding: The ranking above was written before any experiment. The experiment inverted it. Every layer that reads a fault INVENTORY (the given catalogue, USGS QFDB traces, the SGMC map, the GDR thermal springs) is an ANTI-signal on a spatially blocked holdout, because the protocol withholds whole fault segments and buffers the remaining inventory by 300 m: the withheld truth therefore sits in a manufactured gap, and 'distance to the remaining inventory' learns 'gap means no fault'. Measured on the same 2 folds, same 45,000-dot budget, same eligible mask: inventory-based beliefs 0.0178, uniform random 0.0707, inventory-free geophysics and topography 0.17898. The inventory-free stack is 10x the inventory-based one and 2.53x random.
outcome.method_consequence: INVENTORY_LAYERS in src/gems67/design.py is now the single shared exclusion list. Any future recipe in this repository must state whether it reads an inventory, and if it does, it must be compared against the random-placement null before it is believed.
